hero.heading: CC Dental Studio, a cost model sent for correction
hero.caption: Built October 3, 2026, from ccdentalstudio.com, including the staff and testimonial pages, and from public metal prices. No federal index is used, and this page says why. Every number is labeled; the assumptions are sliders; move them and the number moves.
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: (exact: $3,362 and $33,944) Rounding to the nearest $5,000 overstates the low end, so the exact figures govern.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Restorative units you ship in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. With the field empty, the model stays per thousand units.

sliders.label: Units returned by the doctor for remake
sliders.basis: Against a national average near 4 percent, per trade sources [[BENCHMARK]]. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Fully loaded cost of one returned remake
Cases redone inside the laboratory before shipping
sliders.basis: A redo the doctor never sees: caught at the bench, at design, or at the model check. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Share of units that still carry metal
sliders.basis: Metal-free units, zirconia among them, carry no drift. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Metal value in one metal-bearing unit

constants.text: Metal drift uses the public gold price, $4,177 on October 1, 2026 against $3,864 a year earlier (+8.1 percent) [[BENCHMARK]], applied only to units that still carry metal. Zirconia has no public curve and is charged nothing.

model.disclosure: This model carries no federal index: none maps onto a ceramics laboratory.

terms.label: Metal drift on units that still carry metal

model.formulaText: Moved per 1,000 units = 1,000 × returned remake share × remake cost + 1,000 × inside redo share × redo cost + 1,000 × metal share × metal value × 0.081
model.plainText: In words, the remakes your doctors send back at their full cost, plus the redos your bench catches before a case ships, plus the slice of this year's gold rise carried by the units that still hold metal.
model.callout: What nobody writes down is the consistency itself. It lives in your technicians' hands and memories: which doctor wants contacts tight, who wants a shade a half step warmer, how your designer sets a margin. A craft laboratory's consistency is its people, and nobody has written that standard down.

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: You opened the laboratory in 1996 with one stated intent, consistent quality, and thirty years later you publish the people who deliver it: technicians with thirty, thirty, thirty, and twenty-eight years at the bench; the designer who carried the laboratory through CAD [[OBSERVED]].
Two national board certifications, Crown and Bridge and Ceramics, and a director's seat at the state laboratory association [[OBSERVED]].
A dentist of fifteen years calls your communication through every case excellent; another writes that when an emergency collided with her schedule, you and Terri got the case to her [[OBSERVED]].

proposal.heading: What we propose
proposal.lead: The proposal: the count, the consistency file (a build standard per product and a preference profile per doctor, in your technicians' words), and the thirty-day result; fixed fee between $1,200 and $1,800; read-only; no patient information leaves the building.

ledger.title: What a page of the inside redo log looks like
ledger.label: Illustrative, not CC Dental Studio data
ledger.note: Three of five trace to something the consistency file would have written down. Every redo and figure is invented to show the format.

proposal.promise: If your records show our printed range overstated your exposure, our findings letter says so in those words.
